meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_58_packages.json, all reference===58 edges from torahData.js (19 total: 13 bechina, 6 eitza), and the full source text torah_58.txt. For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset and whether it is assigned to a package. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ, נִקְרָא, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת) were considered. Concepts that are pure proof-text citations or causal framings (על ידי) were excluded.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 7 references 'וַיַּרְכֵּב אוֹתוֹ בְּמִרְכֶּבֶת הַמִּשְׁנֶה' (Joseph in the second chariot). This is a proof-text citation supporting the bechina of ברית→לחם משנה, not an independent bechina declaration. The phrase merely illustrates that Joseph who guarded the brit merited the second position.

Joseph is mentioned in section ד as the paradigmatic example of one who guarded the brit. The text says 'וְיוֹסֵף שֶׁזָּכָה לַבְּרִית, כְּתִיב בֵּהּ...' — this is a proof-text citation (כתיב בה = it is written of him), not a bechina declaration (לא נאמר 'זה בחינת יוסף'). Excluded per strict framework rule.

Source text line 18 says 'בְּחִינַת (יְשַׁעְיָה נ"ח): וְקָרָאתָ לַשַּׁבָּת עֹנֶג' — this is a biblical verse cited to show that Shabbat = delight/oneg, which is the source of ahava (love → teshuva from love). 'ענג שבת' is thus cited as a proof-text for the causal chain: oneg shabbat → ahava → teshuva from love. It is a cause-effect link, not a bechina parallel of Shabbat. Excluded.

Lines 22-23 say the 'proper ones of the generation' are beautified ('מַה יָּפִית') as a sign of Torah renewal. The Rebbe uses the verse as illustration, not as an explicit bechina declaration. No 'זה בחינת יופי' statement appears. Excluded.

Line 23 connects הר ציון / גדולה to 'יַרְכְּתֵי צָפוֹן, עַל חַמּוּקֵי יְרֵכַיִךְ, תּוֹרָה הַצְּפוּנָה'. The 'hidden Torah' is the content that the sign/greatness points toward, not a bechina-parallel of greatness itself. The text uses 'ציון וסימן' (sign pointing to), which is closer to an eitza (the greatness is the sign that enables receiving the hidden Torah) than a bechina (same essential nature). Excluded from additions.

Line 9 says 'שְׁתִיָּה כָּלוּל בַּדַּעַת, בִּבְחִינַת (יְשַׁעְיָה נ"ה): הוֹי כָּל צָמֵא לְכוּ לַמַּיִם, שֶׁהִיא בְּאֵר'. This gives שתיה as an aspect of da'at (contained within it) and identifies שתיה=באר. However, the phrase 'כָּלוּל בַּדַּעַת' is not a bechina declaration (it means 'included/contained within'). The relevant bechina is שתיה=באר, but the node 'בְּאֵר מַיִם חַיִּים' is already in Package 1, and 'שתיה' as drinking is better understood as the practical form of that gift. Given that מלבושים is flagged as a gap, שתיה (=function of the water/beer) is a parallel addition candidate, but its bechina language is weaker ('שֶׁהִיא בְּאֵר' = 'which is a well') vs. the explicit 'בְּחִינַת עָנָן בְּחִינַת לְבוּשׁ' for מלבושים. Marginal case; excluded from definitive additions.
